interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland's power grid is currently demonstrating exceptional renewable performance, with regional wind generation standing at a robust 4.4 GW. This surge in zero-carbon supply is driving Scottish carbon intensity down to an impressive 32 gCO2/kWh, reflecting an operational state where fossil-fueled generation has been almost entirely displaced across the regional transmission network. Such low emissions intensity reinforces Scotland’s critical role as the anchor of the broader British clean energy transition.

Despite these strong output indicators, cross-border transmission constraints continue to exert friction on overall system efficiency. Current operational telemetry registers 221.1 MWh of wasted energy, predominantly resulting from curtailment orders deployed to protect the B6 transmission boundary between Scotland and England. While localized thermal saturation forces these dispatch interventions, they highlight a persistent mismatch between peak generation capacity and cross-boundary export infrastructure.

To reduce the economic impact of stranded clean power, grid operators should prioritize dynamic line rating utilization alongside regional battery storage absorption. Incentivizing industrial demand flexibility during these high-wind intervals will also prove vital in curtailing system balancing costs and ensuring Scotland’s low-carbon potential is fully captured rather than throttled.
